claims.text: High-entropy alloys contain multiple principal alloying elements.
HEAs used for thermal insulation typically have random-solid-solution microstructures.
First-principles and simulation methods can provide information about HEA structural properties, pair probabilities, and short-range chemical ordering.
Local chemical-order descriptors can represent relevant ordering and disorder in HEA microstructures.
Integrating ab initio phonon dispersions and microstructural descriptors into machine learning will improve phonon-thermal-conductivity prediction accuracy.
Phonon scattering dominates heat transport from ambient to moderately elevated temperatures in the targeted HEAs.
Local chemical ordering and disorder are associated with anharmonic phonon interactions.
Local chemical order, disorder, and complex microstructure contribute to phonon scattering in HEAs.
Quantitatively representing chemical disorder and microstructural scattering will better resolve microscopic phonon-transport mechanisms.
Better resolution of microscopic phonon-transport mechanisms will yield more accurate thermal-conductivity predictions than simplified scattering models.
Conventional phonon-scattering models omit detailed microstructural descriptors.
The proposed model will markedly reduce thermal-conductivity prediction errors.
The proposed model will reliably identify HEA compositions having a phonon-mean-free-path threshold indicative of low thermal conductivity.
Conventional models consistently misestimate phonon thermal conductivity or mean free path because of oversimplified approximations.
The approach is principally applicable when reliable ab initio phonon data and microstructural descriptors are available.
Performance outside ambient-to-moderate temperatures or for extreme alloy compositions is uncertain.
The magnitude and universality of the improvement depend on the quality and breadth of the input data.
Laser-flash analysis or time-domain thermoreflectance can provide the thermal-conductivity measurements needed for the benchmark.
Failure to significantly outperform conventional models across multiple HEA compositions would falsify the hypothesis.
